reading: The Science History Institute collects, preserves, interprets, and shares the history of science, especially chemistry and the materials that shape everyday life. It is at once a free Philadelphia museum, a research library and archive, a fellowship community, and a publisher of stories, podcasts, and educational activities. It cares about making collections accessible, preserving many kinds of evidence, and questioning tidy accounts of discovery through research and diverse firsthand voices. Its vocabulary runs from alchemy, matter, instruments, rare books, oral histories, and collections to plastics, molecular biology, food science, color, and classroom conflicts. Its distinctive pleasure is the meeting of the strange and the scholarly: a student notebook or obsolete tape can illuminate a scientific life, while a familiar household material connects a museum object to a much larger history.

enemies.idea: A transmutation engine coats every object it catches in brittle gold, leaving the original material trapped inside and demanding more matter for its perfect collection.
enemies.why: The crew can crack the glittering shell to recover useful objects while dodging a machine pursuing an alchemical ideal.

enemies.idea: Firework assemblers pack sparks into scavenged tubes and arrange themselves into elaborate timed displays; their bright patterns signal where the next volley will land.
enemies.why: A historical spectacle becomes a readable, rhythmic fight with a chance to interrupt the sequence.

enemies.idea: A nylon loom unravels natural fibers from clothing and ropes, then spins them into synthetic snares that tighten when pulled.
enemies.why: The nature-to-nylon tour becomes a tactile material puzzle where pulling harder makes escape worse.

enemies.idea: The Notebook Examiner sketches apparatus from student diagrams into three dimensions, but mistakes crossed-out procedures for instructions and unleashes unstable contraptions.
enemies.why: The crew can read the notebook to predict what will appear and cross out a diagram to stop it.

enemies.idea: A tape-spooling scavenger records the crew's movements on obsolete video and plays them back through clattering projector limbs a few seconds later.
enemies.why: Players see their own recent tactics repeated against them and can deliberately record a harmless loop.

enemies.idea: The Utopian Textbook patrol promises a frictionless scientific future, flattening messy rooms and unfinished experiments into glossy, simplified diagrams.
enemies.why: Its idealized diagrams erase useful cover, but anomalies and marginal notes disrupt its tidy view.

enemies.idea: A base-pairing machine tries to match every crew member with a complementary partner, binding mismatched pairs in a twisting ladder until they find the correct release points together.
enemies.why: A molecular motif produces a cooperative positioning problem instead of a generic DNA monster.

enemies.idea: The Photo 51 Sentinel insists one image explains everything; it projects a rigid diffraction pattern that hides earlier evidence and blinds anyone standing in its bright crossings.
enemies.why: Finding the overlooked earlier image gives the crew another angle and breaks the sentinel's certainty.

enemies.idea: A nuclein extractor sorts discarded bandages for hidden material and, having generalized too far, tries to inventory every living cell it encounters.
enemies.why: A discovery in unlikely refuse becomes a scavenger with a clear appetite and distracting decoys.

enemies.idea: The Four-Catalog Hound switches between digital, archival, library, and museum indexes; an object hidden from one nose may be obvious to another.
enemies.why: The absence of one universal search becomes a stealth encounter with four distinct detection rules.

enemies.idea: A reproduction press scans artifacts so aggressively that it removes their fragile surfaces, producing endless imperfect copies to replace the originals.
enemies.why: The crew must protect a delicate original while choosing which copies to sacrifice as decoys.

enemies.idea: The Fellowship Clock grants intruders one to four months, nine months, or two years of artificial research time, accelerating or slowing their movements according to its rotating award dial.
enemies.why: Different fellowship durations become visible timing hazards the crew can manipulate.

enemies.idea: A plastics debate engine makes shields from disposable material while its opposing arms argue whether to keep producing them; each broken shield feeds the next.
enemies.why: The crew must interrupt the cycle rather than simply smash an endless supply of shields.

enemies.idea: Rare-earth prospectors sift floors for trace elements, magnetically pulling tools and machine fragments into a growing mobile ore heap.
enemies.why: Metal equipment becomes both a liability and bait for steering the heap.

enemies.idea: A medicinal-flora stamp press grows paper plants from repeated impressions, then sends thorny roots through cracks to reclaim the ink and paper around it.
enemies.why: A collection of plant stamps becomes a spreading terrain hazard that can be stopped at its press.

enemies.idea: The Color Separator steals pigments from objects and sorts them into marching bands; each band conceals itself against surfaces of its own color.
enemies.why: Changing the surroundings and restoring colors alters what the crew can see.

enemies.idea: The Oral History Splicer cuts invented testimony into convincing fragments and sends them out of sequence to lure travelers down conflicting routes.
enemies.why: Listening for continuity and comparing fragments exposes the machine's false route without impersonating real people.

enemies.idea: The Acquisition Committee sends mechanical calipers to measure anything offered to it, then seizes the donor as missing provenance for the object.
enemies.why: Offering a carefully prepared decoy can occupy the committee long enough for a rescue.

enemies.idea: The Distillation Column boils complicated histories down to one neat answer, releasing clouds that make every witness repeat the same oversimplified account.
enemies.why: Contradictory evidence disrupts the cloud and makes a story about interpretation into a tactical challenge.

enemies.idea: A household-material sorter treats every familiar object as a specimen, stripping useful tools apart to file each component by substance.
enemies.why: Everyday items become vulnerable, encouraging quick improvisation with the material the sorter overlooks.

enemies.idea: A reference automaton answers every question with a question of its own, wrapping the asker in a growing chain of cross-references until someone gives it a genuinely useful clue.
enemies.why: The encounter rewards specificity and turns a research service into a playful interrogation.

enemies.idea: An innovation symposium of rival mechanical lecturers steals techniques from nearby devices, with each speaker demonstrating a new combination before passing it to the next.
enemies.why: Interrupting the handoff prevents abilities from combining and gives the crew a clear target priority.

allies.idea: A surviving reference librarian maps a research question across the separate museum, archive, and library collections, revealing routes the swarm's single-minded search misses.
allies.why: A practical research skill becomes navigation and makes asking a precise question valuable.

allies.idea: A touch-tour guide reads the texture of materials even in darkness and teaches the crew to distinguish harmless old wool from the swarm's synthetic traps.
allies.why: Accessible interpretation offers a useful alternative to relying on sight.

allies.idea: A student notebook preserves failed trials alongside results; its anonymous annotations show which of the swarm's reconstructed apparatus will collapse safely.
allies.why: The messy record of learning becomes a field guide to disabling enemies.

allies.idea: A conservator with a hand-cranked player rescues evidence from obsolete tapes before the swarm can overwrite them, trading recovered clues for replacement parts.
allies.why: Preservation is an active rescue mission with a tangible reward.

allies.idea: A gallery guide leads small groups through a free refuge, using familiar household materials to improvise shields and explain safe routes.
allies.why: The museum's welcoming mission survives as practical help grounded in its materials collection.

bosses.idea: The Grand Curator has fused alchemical furnaces, archival cabinets, specimen instruments, and playback machines into a walking museum. It collects, preserves, interprets, and shares by trapping everything, freezing it, assigning one meaning, and broadcasting that meaning everywhere.
bosses.why: Each phase twists one part of the institute's mission; freeing varied evidence weakens the whole machine.

bosses.idea: The Universal Catalogue attempts to force books, instruments, oral histories, and artwork into one perfect index. It reconfigures the room whenever something refuses its classification, compressing contradictory objects into a single entry.
bosses.why: The diversity of the collection drives a shifting arena, and preserving incompatible kinds of evidence defeats its false order.

bosses.idea: The Philosopher's Archive seeks the ultimate explanation of matter, combining alchemical transformation with molecular models and mechanically edited histories. Each supposedly final answer changes the arena's materials until the crew exposes an overlooked observation.
bosses.why: The site's long arc from alchemy to modern inquiry becomes a multi-stage argument fought through matter and evidence.

events.idea: A crate of nonperishable food is stranded behind a machine sorting station. The crew can divert the sorter with empty tins and carry the supplies to a waiting neighborhood pantry.
events.why: A small act of mutual aid gives the crew a concrete objective amid the invasion.

events.idea: A guided tea gathering has become a chemical guessing game: a kettle machine only opens the exit after the crew identifies which safe household material changed the water's color.
events.why: Cuppa Chemistry becomes a low-stakes observational puzzle.

events.idea: A pair of competing diffraction projections blocks a corridor. Comparing the earlier image with the celebrated later one reveals a gap that either image alone conceals.
events.why: The value of revisiting evidence becomes a spatial puzzle.

events.idea: A library cart has spilled books, objects, and recordings into one pile; four small sorting machines each demand a different kind of item before they will open their respective doors.
events.why: Sorting mixed collections offers multiple routes and rewards inspecting the objects.

events.idea: A scholar's timed fellowship chamber is about to seal with a precious notebook inside. The crew can reset its duration dial, but each longer interval wakes another clockwork attendant.
events.why: A choice between more time and more opposition gives the rescue a concrete tradeoff.

events.idea: A textile tour has left a trail of wool and nylon samples across a dark room. A guide asks the crew to find a route by touch before a loom takes the samples away.
events.why: Different material textures become navigational clues.

events.idea: A damaged tape contains a vital view of a corridor, but its player is missing a wheel. The crew can borrow a part from a nearby patrol, then watch the recording to time their crossing.
events.why: Restoring obsolete playback has an immediate practical payoff.

events.idea: A machine has staged a role-playing debate over plastics and refuses to release a trapped object until someone presents two different uses and consequences from the scattered exhibit materials.
events.why: The classroom's structured conflict becomes an exploration challenge with more than one perspective.

events.idea: A laboratory notebook's apparatus drawing has been built incorrectly by the swarm. Reconnecting it according to the student's annotations safely vents a locked chamber.
events.why: Reading a historical working document directly changes the physical environment.

events.idea: An alchemical painting machine is turning a pile of ordinary tools gold. The crew can save one tool before the next transformation, while a second remains trapped behind a fragile gilded shell.
events.why: A quick choice makes the alchemical theme matter to the crew's equipment.

events.idea: A box of medicinal-plant stamps is scattering paper leaves through a ventilation shaft. Returning the matching impressions to their botanical outlines opens a sheltered passage.
events.why: Matching plant images gives a quiet collecting task a useful destination.

events.idea: A researcher asks for a reproduction of a fragile object, but the swarm's scanner will damage it. The crew can adjust the light and distance to capture a legible image while keeping the original intact.
events.why: The tension between access and physical preservation becomes a hands-on challenge.

events.idea: A free gallery tour is stranded by a shifting route through matter and materials. The crew can escort the visitors by following material samples left by their guide.
events.why: A group visit becomes a compact escort with an environmental trail.

events.idea: A food-technology demonstration machine keeps presenting strange imaginary meals. One harmless sample attracts a patrol, while another can be used to lure it away from a trapped cart.
events.why: Food innovation becomes a playful experiment in creature behavior.

events.idea: Two fictional oral-history fragments disagree about the location of a lost instrument. Listening to the surrounding context reveals that they describe the same room before and after it was rearranged.
events.why: Apparent contradiction becomes a clue to change over time.

events.idea: A resource guide points to minerals, color, food, and fireworks. Four corresponding sample drawers hide parts of a key, but opening the fireworks drawer first triggers a noisy display.
events.why: The guide's varied topics become an optional scavenger hunt with a readable consequence.
